question: For a Automotive use case involving automotive radar, where would Oscilloscope fit in the test workflow?
answer: In the Vault the automotive-radar anchor is the R&S AREG800A Automotive Radar Echo Generator, which stimulates a radar under test by generating dynamic artificial objects (echoes) — so the oscilloscope is not the stimulus instrument but an optional downstream analysis instrument. It fits at the AREG800A's auxiliary IF output, enabled by the R&S AREG8-K740 option: the datasheet states the auxiliary receive signal IF output at the AREG800A base unit is 'for optional signal analysis: connect to a spectrum analyzer or oscilloscope'. Its documented purpose there is radar signal analysis and EIRP measurements, i.e. you tap the radar-under-test's received/downconverted signal at IF rather than probing 77 GHz RF directly. Practical constraints from the specs: the AUX IF output measurement port is max. 0 dBm, gain is 0 dB (nom.) from RX IF input to AUX IF output at the base unit (12 dB nom. at the frontend variants), and the AUX IF output frequency range depends on frontend/option (e.g. 1.1–2.1 GHz, 0.7–4.7 GHz or 0.7–5.7 GHz for 77/79 GHz frontends, 700–950 MHz for 24 GHz frontends) — so the scope only needs to cover the IF band, not the mmWave RF. Note the parallel but distinct path: power and EIRP measurements at the RX power connector on the mmWave frontend module are made with a power sensor, not a scope. Beyond this interface the Vault does not describe a stage-by-stage automotive radar test workflow (R&D vs. HiL vs. production), although it does record the AREG8-K109 hardware-in-the-loop control interface and production frontend/base-unit options as other workflow elements.
missing: The Vault has no oscilloscope product pages (no R&S RTO/RTP/MXO entity or source notes), so it gives no scope model, bandwidth, sampling-rate or probing recommendations, and no automotive-radar-specific scope application note. It also contains no documented end-to-end automotive radar test workflow (R&D / HiL / validation / production stages) in which to place the oscilloscope; the placement above is inferred only from the AREG800A datasheet's AUX IF output interface description.
